reference.title: Band Standing Single Arm Row
reference.listing: Animated GIF (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row, breathe in as the arm reaches forward.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s row, short squeeze, about 2 s back

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer squeeze, a step farther from the rack, then the next band up.

cues.text: Staggered stance facing a rack, left foot forward, knees soft, trunk tall. The band is looped round the upright at about waist-to-chest height; hold it in the right hand, arm straight toward the upright, palm facing in. Left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and drive the elbow back close to the side until the hand reaches the lower ribs.
Squeeze the shoulder blade toward the spine; hips and shoulders square to the rack.
Breathe in and let the arm reach forward under control, the shoulder blade gliding forward at the end.
Short pause with the band taut, then row again.

mistakes.mistake: Rotating the trunk to finish the row
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders square; brace against the twist.
Pull the elbow back and down.
Keep the elbow close to the side.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back as the band tightens
mistakes.fix: Stand tall over the front foot.

kinematics.norm: Elbow travels straight back close to the side (clinical opinion)
Nearly straight in front to about 100-120 degrees at the ribs, the forearm staying in line with the band (clinical opinion)
Protracted at the reach, retracted at the end of the row (clinical opinion)
Staggered, opposite foot forward; standing one-arm pulls raise trunk muscle activity (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012; Fenwick 2009).
Elastic resistance can give muscle activity comparable to free weights at a matched effort (Andersen 2010).
About 1 s row and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Standing Single Arm Row, animated GIF (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Low back: keep the trunk tall rather than leaning back against the band (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Balance: square stance with the feet hip width.
regressions: Lighter band or step closer to the rack.
progressions: Stronger band or step farther away.
One-arm dumbbell row or one-arm cable row.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Extend the shoulder as the elbow drives back (Lehman 2004).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Retract the shoulder blade at the end of the row.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Extends the arm behind the body.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the one-arm pull twisting the trunk (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012 found more trunk activity with unilateral and standing exercises).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the one-arm pull twisting the trunk (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012 found more trunk activity with unilateral and standing exercises).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the pelvis in the staggered stance.
